- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or volatile, model over-anticipates corrections; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days by 15–30%.
- Model often overshoots after a spike in sentiment (e.g., +0.67 → +1.00), leading to over-forecasting in next 5 days; apply 15–25% downward correction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model fails to adjust; apply upward bias correction starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); add 5–10% upward bias to forecast for days 15–25.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.33 or below) over 5+ days, model under-forecasts; apply 10–20% upward bias for next 7 days.
- Model tends to lag in response to sentiment spikes; if sentiment rises sharply (e.g., from 0.33 to 1.00 in 2 days), forecast should be adjusted upward by 10–20% for next 3 days.
